cells.tense: Right now you're stepping forward without needing to see the whole way, and the not-seeing isn't costing you anything.
cells.ask: Pick the next real step and take it from how you actually feel about it — let the momentum come out of that, once, today.
cells.core:
You can walk into what isn't clear yet, and you do it calmly. You let go of the old shape of something — a plan, a role, a way you used to be needed — and the ground stays under you while you do it. What you picture ahead is made of what you've already lived through, so it holds weight. You're not dreaming instead of living; you're dreaming from having lived, and the difference shows in how steady you are.

The next thing already has a direction in it. You don't have to find it by thinking harder. Move on the one you're drawn to and let that motion carry you — the step is enough for now.
cells.sheetLine: You step into the unclear without forcing it, and your grip opens without losing you the ground.

cells.tense: You're living a few turns ahead of where you actually are, and the version you're rehearsing has started to feel like the real one.
cells.ask: Today, tend one thing that's actually in front of you — give it what it needs and stop there, no push past what it can take.
cells.core:
Picturing what comes next is a real gift when it stays tied to what's here. When it doesn't, the picture stops being a picture. You read signs into everything, half of them you put there, and you've started steering by a meaning you can't check against anything in the room. What you're trying to hold together is more than holding together, and the effort is making it worse.

Go back to what's actually growing — a person, a project, a practice — something small and alive. Pay attention to what it needs rather than what you need it to become. Care that doesn't exhaust itself leaves both of you somewhere new.

cells.tense: You stopped taking the unclear seriously a while back, and you're still standing where you stopped.
cells.ask: Notice one thing today that doesn't fit into plain facts, and let yourself know it before you can explain it — that's the whole of it.
cells.core:
You can let something be unfinished and stay easy about it. You can walk toward what you don't understand yet without needing it explained first — not-knowing doesn't scare you, it just means there's more. What you sense about a situation can arrive before you can argue for it, and it usually turns out right. Letting go gets easier too, because you're not gripping something you can't name.

That channel is quiet right now. You want the literal version of everything, plain and testable, and anything that only shows up as a hunch or an image gets waved off. The big picture has gone flat. Nothing's wrong with your mind — you've just stopped letting it know things it can't prove yet.

cells.tense: It's happening now — you're already shaping what your life is reaching for, and you're telling the story as though it's reaching for you.
cells.ask: Once today, do one small thing the same way twice on purpose — a practice, not a performance — and let that be the whole of it.
cells.core:
When you're inside it, you know what you're working toward and you can say so. You can picture the life you're building and let that picture steer the ordinary day, not just the big moments. What you imagine organizes what you do, and letting go of the rest gets simpler because you know what you're keeping.

You're doing that already. Something ahead has your hours aimed at it — the shape of it is in your choices, in where your attention keeps drifting, in the hours you spend rehearsing a version of things. You talk about it like weather. A small steady practice, kept up without needing it to prove anything, is how you get to say what it's for.
